subject: Terminal Delight keeps a relationship builder above its agent chart and submits multiple targets and staged pool members together.
reader: Parker requested these changes and already uses the Threshing Floor, its chart, pane pool, organisations, filter and Ops skin. He wants to judge the native result and its validation; source and build details are optional provenance.

sections.heading: Relationship builder
sections.text:
In Terminal Delight, dragging one agent card onto another previously left you without a usable relationship builder. The new builder stays above the chart: choose the acting agent, what it can do and the target agents, then Submit. Pool cards join the org only on submission. 
 Built and staged Both terminal cores checked

 Opening and cancelling a draft preserve the chart, pool and composer bounds. This is the staged binary rendered in a disposable native window using your Ops skin. sections.heading: Cancellation and limits
sections.text:
03 · An invalid target stops the whole save 
 | 
 | Action or condition | Verified result 

 | Card onto another card | Actor and target fill the builder; permission awaits a chosen verb and Submit. 

 | Alt + left drag | A tether is drawn; the source card stays fixed. An invalid destination changes no membership. 

 | Cancel the draft | Staged pool cards remain in the pool; the filter stays intact. 

 | A target disappears, changes org or has conflicting membership | The draft remains visible, an error identifies the affected selection, and nothing is committed. 

 | Self-target or duplicate | Selection and batch validation reject it. 

 | Read-only or off-limits pane | The existing pane limits still control access; adding membership does not open the pane. 

 The final native view pass finished with 44 passing checks. Full suites passed 3,000 tests on the default core and 2,947 on Alacritty, with 17 existing ignored tests per run. Formatting, the CI Clippy commands on both cores, and the optimized build passed. The capture shows the resting layout; drag and batch behavior are verified by native input tests.
